question:
**Fill in the blanks:**

Zonal Councils were created by the ______ Act, 1956.
solution:
The correct answer is __**States Reorganisation Act, 1956**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Zonal Councils in India were established under the **States Reorganisation Act, 1956**, which aimed to reorganize states based on linguistic and administrative considerations.
 
• The primary objective of Zonal Councils was to foster **cooperation and coordination among states and Union Territories** in a particular zone.
 
• There are **five Zonal Councils**—Northern, Central, Eastern, Western, and Southern—each comprising states grouped based on geographical proximity.
 
• The Zonal Councils are chaired by the **Union Home Minister** and include the Chief Ministers of the member states, along with other ministers as representatives.
 
• Zonal Councils serve as a platform to resolve inter-state disputes and promote regional development by addressing common issues such as economic planning, border disputes, and cultural exchanges.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Finance Commission**

 
 
• The Finance Commission is constituted under Article 280 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It is primarily responsible for **dividing tax revenues between the Central and State governments** and addressing financial relations between them.
 
• The Finance Commission is appointed every five years, and its recommendations are advisory in nature.
 
• It does not pertain to the creation of Zonal Councils but plays a crucial role in managing fiscal matters in federal governance.
 
 
 
• **Panchayati Raj**
 
 
• The Panchayati Raj system was introduced as a form of **decentralized governance** under Article 40 of the Directive Principles of State Policy in the Constitution.
 
• The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, provided constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions.
 
• It focuses on grassroots-level governance and local self-government but does not relate to Zonal Councils.
 
 
 
• **Representation of the People Act**
 
 
• The Representation of the People Act, 1951, governs the conduct of elections in India.
 
• It provides provisions for the qualification and disqualification of Members of Parliament and State Legislatures.
 
• While it is critical in ensuring free and fair elections, it is unrelated to the establishment of Zonal Councils.
